Where Exa holds up, and where it does not

Each bar is how much of the category-leading score Exa reaches. This is the number that decides whether routing around it is worth anything.

Share of the best score

by category
Bars start at 70%. The accent marks categories below 90% of the best available score.

A vendor that trails overall can still be the right call for one kind of query. That is why scores are reported per category. The four routing cases read straight off these bars.

Every category

Exa, category by category

Sample size is published beside every score. A cell below the coverage floor is shown as missing rather than as a number computed from a thin sample.

Score is the mean of the ensemble medians in that category. "Of best" is the share of the category-leading score.

Known limits

Read this

of data. Scores carry roughly points of judge-to-judge disagreement and the judge families differ by points on the same responses, so the ranking is the finding and the absolute score is not. There is no human-labelled calibration set yet. The full list of limitations.

One configuration is measured. If it misrepresents Exa — wrong tier, depth or parameters — corrections get a changelog entry, not a silent edit. Report it, or recompute it from the export.
